why: DECISION_RULES requires candidate configs, opponent panel, seeds, seats, game counts, metric and confidence calculations, package latency budget, the H4 blend alpha and the MCTS override thresholds to be frozen before final results. Registering afterwards would permit selecting whichever configuration flattered the outcome.
games_per_pair_rationale: CONTRACT §9 requires >=800 common-panel baseline-vs-corrected-MCTS games (100/pair x 4 opponents x 2 candidates = 800), >=200 final-panel games per promotable hybrid mode (50/pair x 4 = 200), and >=40 diagnostic games for non-promotable H2-H4 (satisfied by the same 200). Controls are sampled at 25/pair because no floor requires more and their search cost is real.
seat_assignment: alternating by pair index; identical across candidates
seed_rule: seed = 20260728 + opponent_index*1000 + pair_index -- depends only on the pair, so every candidate meets the same agent-side seed schedule
environment_randomness_note: make("cabt") exposes actTimeout/episodeSteps/runTimeout but NO seed, so shuffles and coin flips are not paired between candidates. Differences smaller than the reported Wilson interval are not attributable to the candidate.
metric: field score = mean per-game score (win 1.0, draw 0.5, loss 0.0) over all opponents
confidence: Wilson score interval at z=1.96, reported per matchup and for the field

c019_control_config.note: the configuration at which c019 measured its own gate

execution_note: The panel is executed in two batches to use capacity while ByteRL training completes: batch A covers the six candidates that do not depend on the c020 ByteRL checkpoint (baseline, three c019 controls, corrected MCTS, H0), batch B the five that do. The protocol above is frozen before EITHER batch runs, aggregates are computed once from the merged raw games, and no candidate's configuration differs between batches. Environment randomness is already documented as unpairable across candidates, so batching does not remove a guarantee the panel otherwise had.
